title: Drip-Drop, Abba Hilkiah!
summary: In a little village there is no rain, the field is thirsty and the cow is yawning. The sages send two of their number to ask Abba Hilkiah, grandson of Honi the Circle-Maker, to pray. But Abba Hilkiah just works in silence, doesn't look up, doesn't answer... Drip-drop? Not a single drop! Until he and his wife quietly climb up to the roof, and two little clouds appear. A rhyming story about humility, quiet work and a warm home, based on the legend in Tractate Taanit.
pages:
In a little village, the sun beat down, blazing hot,
The ground was cracked and thirsty, thirsty a lot.
The cow was yawning, the cat ready to flop —
Drip-drop? None! Not a single drop!

The sages sat and thought: what can we do?
"Let's send two sages, let's send two!
Let them go to Abba Hilkiah, his house isn't far away,
He's a quiet man, simple and humble and good in every way."

The two sages went, with a walking stick and a hat,
They knocked on the door: knock-knock! And nobody answered that.
The house was quiet, the garden dry... where is he? Where? Don't stop!
Drip-drop? None! Not a single drop!

They found him in the field, with a hoe in his hand,
Digging and digging, not resting a moment on the land.
"Shalom!" said the tall one, in a voice small and kind.
And Abba Hilkiah? Kept digging. Didn't look up, didn't mind.

"SHALOM!!!" yelled the short one, loud as a drum,
BOOM-BOOM! "SHALOM!!!" And Abba Hilkiah? Dug on till the work was done.
And the sun up above was laughing, hot and bright on top —
Drip-drop? None! Not a single drop!

In the evening he carried wood on one shoulder,
And his cloak on the other, carefully, as the day grew older.
And the sages behind him, puffing, in a line:
"Well? Maybe now?" Silence. Just a bird singing fine.

At home his wife was waiting, in a pretty dress,
With a scarf on her head and a smile, no less.
He handed out bread: one slice for the older son,
And two for the little one! As hungry as a bird, that one.

And Abba Hilkiah whispered, "They came because of the rain, I know.
Let's go up to the roof and pray, and maybe God will hear us below."
They climbed up quietly, each to a corner of their own,
He in this corner, and she in the other, alone.

And suddenly, above her corner: POOF! A little cloud came,
And above his corner: POOF! Another white cloud, just the same.
The sages cried, "It's thanks to you, Abba Hilkiah!"
And he only smiled: "Thanks to Heaven... and thanks to her!"

In the little village, the sun went off to rest,
The ground was drinking, the field blooming its best.
The cow in a puddle, the cat wet and pretty, on top —
Drip-drop? Yes! Another drop and another drop!
